info.title: SoChain API
info.summary: Balances, transactions, blocks, the mempool, prices and charts for Bitcoin, Litecoin, Dogecoin, Zcash and their testnets.
info.description:
SoChain API v3. Lookups work without a key. Send your key in the `API-KEY` header (`X-API-Key` or `Authorization: Bearer` also work) for your plan's monthly requests, and for buckets, webhooks, /account_info and /support, which always need one (without it they answer 401: "This endpoint needs an API key: send it as the API-KEY header.").

Answers are JSON: `{"status": "success", "data": …}` or `{"status": "fail", "data": {"error_message": "…"}}`; only `/account_info` answers without the envelope, and `format=csv` history exports are CSV. A method an endpoint doesn't take answers 405, naming the ones it does ("This endpoint takes GET."); GET on the base URL answers where the docs, this document and MCP are. Amounts are exact 8-decimal strings, times Unix seconds, hashes lowercase hex (any case is read). Prices are in US dollars, or the currency you ask for: always 0 on testnets, and null on a mainnet where there's no price (before its price history, or a block stamped ahead of the clock). An answer a few blocks behind carries a Warning header ("1 block behind: answered as of block 971060"), and one without its prices "Warning: price unavailable".

Networks: BTC, LTC, DOGE, ZEC (Zcash), BTCTEST (Bitcoin testnet4), LTCTEST (Litecoin testnet4), DOGETEST (Dogecoin testnet) and ZECTEST (Zcash testnet). On Zcash, the transparent side only.

Limits: without a key, lookups are 2,500 a UTC day per IP (an IPv6 /48 counts as one), API and MCP together; past that they answer 429, and more needs a key. Paid plans have reserved capacity and are served first when it's busy. With a key, requests per calendar month (UTC) by plan: Free 75,000, Hobby 500,000, Starter 1,500,000, Professional 15,000,000, Behemoth 150,000,000. Past the month's quota, lookups carry on at the keyless rate (still 200, with X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0) while webhooks and streams pause until the 1st or an upgrade; once that rate is used up too, keyed calls answer 401. Answers carry X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining and X-RateLimit-Reset (seconds until the count resets: the month with a key, the UTC day without); 401, 403 and 429 refusals don't.

Live WebSocket streams (every paid plan) are at /api/v3/stream on the same host, with the same key. The same data is available to AI agents over MCP at https://sochain.com/mcp with the same key and limits.

Webhook deliveries carry SoChain-Signature: verify it before trusting a payload, and reply with any 2xx within 30 seconds, or the delivery is retried.

get.summary: Whether a transaction is pending, mined, replaced or dropped
get.description: A transaction is replaced when another one spends one of its inputs (a fee bump, a double spend, or a transaction it spends from being replaced) and dropped when the mempool lets it go unconfirmed. SoChain remembers a transaction that left the mempool for about a day; after that, or for one SoChain never saw, the status is unknown.

post.description: A support request about your key's account; a person replies by email. Any key may send one, read-only too, and it's never counted. The account's failed calls and webhook deliveries from the last 24 hours are attached unless include_recent_failures is false. A message containing a key or recovery phrase is refused. Also available as the MCP tool contact_support.

post.summary: Add a wallet's addresses from its public key
post.description: Send a wallet's extended public key and SoChain adds its used addresses on the receive and change chains, plus `spare` unused ones after the last used (default 20). The bucket is made if it doesn't exist (then network is needed). Sending the same public key again adds newly used addresses and tops the spare ones up; another wallet's key is refused (409). The public key is used for this request only and not kept: the bucket keeps addresses, positions and the key's fingerprint. A private key (xprv…) is refused. Single-key wallets (BIP44/49/84/86).

network.description: Needed when the bucket doesn't exist yet.

type.description: Implied by a ypub, zpub, upub, vpub or Mtub. A plain xpub, tpub, Ltub, ttub or dgub is used for every type: say which, or leave it out and the type the wallet has used is picked (a wallet with no history yet needs it).

ApiKeyQuery.name: api_key
ApiKeyQuery.description: Your key as a URL parameter, for lookups (GET) from tools that can't send a header, such as spreadsheets. Best a read-only key.

page.name: page
page.description: Page number from 1; ten results per page. Anything but a 1–6 digit number means page 1.

hash_or_height.name: hash_or_height
hash_or_height.description: A block height (up to 8 digits) or block hash (64 hex characters, any case).

unix_timestamp.name: unix_timestamp
unix_timestamp.description: Unix seconds (7–10 digits): the price at that time. Anything else means the latest price.

interval.name: interval
interval.description: Not every series has every interval: block and hour/day for most; minute only for tx_per_min, mempool_txs and mempool_bytes.

from.name: from
from.description: Start of the range, inclusive: a block height for the block interval, else Unix seconds (rounded down to the start of its minute, hour or day, and no earlier than the network's first block).

to.name: to
to.description: End of the range, inclusive, in the same units. Defaults to now; later times are now, and heights stop at the tip. Times are rounded down like from.

SignatureHeader.name: SoChain-Signature
SignatureHeader.description: t=<unix time>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of t + "." + raw body, keyed with your webhook secret>. Reject anything older than 5 minutes; compare in constant time.

DeliveryHeader.name: SoChain-Delivery
DeliveryHeader.description: This delivery's ID; retries repeat it.

height.name: height
height.description: The confirmed balance at the end of this block, instead of now.

time.name: time
time.description: The confirmed balance at this time, instead of now: Unix seconds, a UTC date (meaning the end of that day) or an RFC 3339 timestamp. It's taken at the last block at or before it. Not together with height.

from_height.name: from_height
from_height.description: History filter: from this block on (inclusive).

to_height.name: to_height
to_height.description: History filter: up to this block (inclusive).

from_time.name: from_time
from_time.description: History filter: from this time on. Unix seconds, a UTC date (from its first second) or an RFC 3339 timestamp.

to_time.name: to_time
to_time.description: History filter: up to this time. Unix seconds, a UTC date (to its last second) or an RFC 3339 timestamp. Times map to the blocks they cover, so back-to-back ranges neither overlap nor leave a gap.

direction.name: direction
direction.description: History filter: in (the balance went up), out (it went down) or both. By the net amount: a payment out with change back counts once, as out.

unconfirmed.name: unconfirmed
unconfirmed.description: History filter: pending transactions. Default include, or exclude when the range has an end (to_height or to_time), which can't be combined with include or only.

page_size.name: page_size
page_size.description: Rows per page of the filtered form: 1–100 (default 10); with format=csv 1–500 (default 500).

cursor.name: cursor
cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous page of the filtered form. It carries the filters, so it can be sent on its own.

format.name: format
format.description: json (default) or csv. CSV has one row per transaction (time_utc, block, txid, direction, received, sent, net, price_usd, net_usd); the next page's URL is in the Link header.

members.name: members
members.description: With height or time: each address's balance too.

currency.name: currency
currency.description: Prices in this currency instead of US dollars (any case). Not a filter: on the paged endpoints it keeps the form you'd get without it.

history_interval.name: interval
history_interval.description: One point per day (default), week (Monday to Sunday, UTC) or month.

history_from.name: from
history_from.description: Start: Unix seconds, a UTC date (from its first second) or an RFC 3339 timestamp. Default: the address's first activity (without an API key, daily points cover the most recent 2,000).

history_to.name: to
history_to.description: End, in the same forms (a date means its last second). Default: now.

Unauthorized.description: An invalid key, no key where one is needed (buckets, webhooks, /account_info), a locked account or expired plan, or both the month's requests and the keyless rate used up. Kept as 401, with this message, for v3 compatibility.

data.error_message: API Key invalid, account access expired, or this account's daily request limit has been exhausted.

TooManyRequests.description: Without a key, past the day's 2,500 lookups from this IP while SoChain is busy (Retry-After: 60), or past the day's most (Retry-After: seconds to 00:00 UTC). With or without one, too many requests in flight at once (Retry-After: 1, not counted).

data.error_message: Lookups without a key are 2,500 a day per IP, and today's are used up; they reset at 00:00 UTC. A free API key gives you 75,000 a month: https://sochain.com/signin?from=limit

Unavailable.description: Briefly unavailable; retry with backoff. May carry Retry-After.

data.error_message: Temporarily unavailable. Try again in a few minutes.

BadRequest.description: A bad parameter or body; the message says which.

Busy.description: Address changes are paced: up to 10,000 accepted changes a second per account on each network, within a network-wide cap. Wait the Retry-After seconds and send the same call again.

data.error_message: This account is adding and removing addresses faster than 10,000 a second on BTC. Try again in a second.

Forbidden.description: A read-only key, or a change past your plan's limits: data.error_message says which.

NotJson.description: A body that isn't JSON: send it with Content-Type: application/json.

TooLarge.description: A body over the limit: 256 KB where a call carries addresses or transaction IDs, 64 KB otherwise.

Amount.description: An exact decimal amount of coins with 8 decimals. Signed amounts may start with '-'. Parse as an integer of the smallest unit, not a float.

Price.description: Price per coin, 8 decimals: in US dollars, or in the currency asked for. Always 0.00000000 on testnets.

currency.description: USD, or the currency asked for.

unconfirmed.description: Pending change from the mempool. Can be negative.

txs_sent.description: Transactions in which the address sent coins.

txs_received.description: Transactions in which it received coins.

txs_total.description: Every transaction it appears in, each counted once.

first_active.description: The block of its first transaction; null for an address with none.

last_active.description: The block of its latest transaction; null for an address with none.

block.description: Height of the confirming block; null while unconfirmed.

price.description: The price at the time, as Price; null where there's no price: before the network's price history (Bitcoin's starts 13 Jul 2010), or a block stamped ahead of the clock. Testnets: always 0.

p2pk.description: DOGE only: present when the entry involves one of the key's pay-to-pubkey scripts.

transactions.description: Up to 10 per page: unconfirmed first, then newest first.

hash.description: The transaction that created the output.

index.description: The output's position in that transaction.

block.description: Confirming block height; null while unconfirmed.

p2pk.description: DOGE only: the output is a pay-to-pubkey script of the address's key.

outputs.description: Up to 10 per page, oldest first.

address.description: Null for a coinbase or a script without an address.

sequence.description: The input's nSequence: 4294967295 is final; below 4294967294 signals replace-by-fee where the network allows it, and it can set a relative timelock (BIP 68).

mweb.description: Litecoin only: pool when it spends the MWEB pool, pegin when it spends a peg-in. Absent otherwise.

address.description: "op_return" for an OP_RETURN (nulldata) output, as v3 always said; null for other nonstandard scripts.

type.description: pubkeyhash, scripthash, witness_v0_keyhash, witness_v0_scripthash, witness_v1_taproot, nulldata, …

spent.description: The spending input; null while unspent.

is_change.description: true when it pays one of the transaction's own input addresses; otherwise null (never false).

mweb.description: Litecoin only: pegin (moves coins into MWEB), pool (the MWEB pool, carried to the next block) or pegout (coins leaving MWEB). Absent otherwise.

price.description: The price at the time, as Price; null where there's no price: before the network's price history (Bitcoin's starts 13 Jul 2010), or a block stamped ahead of the clock. Testnets: always 0.

facts.description: Only for a bridge's or a protocol's transaction: the name of its bridge (sBTC, Liquid, …) or protocol (babylon, counterparty, …).

kind.description: What kind of transaction it is (inscription, rune, …), named as in a block's kinds (BlockKinds says what each is); null when not classified.

heuristic.description: true when the kind is a guess (a CoinJoin, a cooperative Lightning close, a child paying its parent's fee); null with no kind.

mweb.description: Litecoin only: hogex for each block's MWEB transaction (its first output is the pool), pegin when it moves coins into MWEB. Absent otherwise.

shielded.description: Zcash only: the value each shielded pool released into the transparent side (positive) or took from it (negative). Shielded inputs and outputs themselves are private: inputs and outputs list the transparent side only, and fee already accounts for this.

status.description: pending: waiting in the mempool. mined: in a block. replaced: another transaction spends one of its inputs. dropped: it left the mempool unconfirmed. expired (Zcash): it passed its expiry height unmined. unknown: SoChain can't tell (it never saw it, or it left the mempool too long ago).

block_height.description: The block it's in, once mined.

confirmations.description: 0 while pending, 1 or more once mined; null otherwise.

replaced_by.description: The transaction that now spends one of its inputs (the last one, after several quick replacements).

replaced_by_status.description: unknown: the replacement left the mempool unconfirmed too.

replaced_ancestor.description: Set when it was replaced because a transaction it spends from was: that transaction.

removed_at.description: When it left the mempool (Unix time).

nonce.description: The header's nonce. On Zcash (ZEC, ZECTEST), a string: its 32-byte Equihash nonce in hex.

min_fee_rate.description: The lowest fee rate its transactions paid, rounded up to a whole unit: sat/vB on BTC, lit/vB on LTC, koinu/vB on DOGE, zat/action on ZEC. The coinbase isn't counted; on Litecoin, MWEB's HogEx transaction, peg-ins and transactions spending MWEB coins aren't either. Null for a block with only its coinbase.

median_fee_rate.description: The median fee rate (with an even count, the lower of the two middle rates), in the same units and with the same exclusions as min_fee_rate.

max_fee_rate.description: The highest fee rate, in the same units and with the same exclusions as min_fee_rate.

min_fee_rate_precise.description: min_fee_rate to two decimal places, not rounded up ("0.31"). Null where not available yet, which includes most blocks mined before 5 October 2026.

median_fee_rate_precise.description: median_fee_rate to two decimal places; null as for min_fee_rate_precise.

max_fee_rate_precise.description: max_fee_rate to two decimal places; null as for min_fee_rate_precise.

reward_split.description: Zcash (ZEC) only: where the reward went. Amounts are decimal strings.

nsm_fee_contribution.description: From the NU7 upgrade (ZECTEST today): the 60% of fees burned into the NSM reserve; 0 before it.

txs.description: Every transaction ID, in block order.

price.description: The price at the time, as Price; null where there's no price: before the network's price history (Bitcoin's starts 13 Jul 2010), or a block stamped ahead of the clock. Testnets: always 0.

median_time.description: The median time of this block and the 10 before it (Unix time); null for an orphaned Zcash block.

chainwork.description: The chain's total expected work up to this block, 64 hex characters; null on ZEC and ZECTEST.

stripped_size.description: Size without witness data, in bytes; null on DOGE, DOGETEST, ZEC and ZECTEST.

mweb.description: Litecoin only, from MWEB's activation. value_out includes the pool carried over from block to block; subtract pool for the value the block moved.

auxpow.description: Dogecoin (DOGE, DOGETEST), a merge-mined block: the Litecoin block attempt whose proof of work it reuses. null on every other block.

parent_hash.description: The parent header's hash: the Litecoin block hash it has, or would have had.

parent_chain.description: LTC (LTCTEST on DOGETEST) when the parent builds on a Litecoin block; null otherwise.

parent_in_chain.description: Whether the attempt became a Litecoin block; null until that's known.

parent_height.description: Its Litecoin height, when parent_in_chain is true.

price.description: The price at the time, as Price; null where there's no price: before the network's price history (Bitcoin's starts 13 Jul 2010), or a block stamped ahead of the clock. Testnets: always 0.

miner.description: Address paid by the coinbase, usually the pool's payout address.

BlockKinds.description: A block's transactions by kind, each by name. Every transaction counts, under one kind, except the coinbase (and Litecoin's HogEx); a kind with none is left out. null or absent for a block whose kinds aren't known yet. coinjoin, a cooperative lightning_close and a fee_bumped child paying its parent's fee are told by their shape alone: likely, not certain.

payment.description: An ordinary payment, and anything that isn't another kind. BTC, LTC, DOGE.

batch_payout.description: One sender paying many at once: exchanges, payroll. BTC, LTC, DOGE.

consolidation.description: Many coins merged into one or two, often while fees are low. BTC, LTC, DOGE.

coinjoin.description: Many people mixing equal amounts. BTC, LTC.

inscription.description: Content, such as an image or text, inscribed on chain: ordinals and Atomicals, and Doginals on Dogecoin. BTC, LTC, DOGE.

data.description: Records in OP_RETURN outputs: timestamps, proofs. BTC, LTC, DOGE.

lightning_close.description: A Lightning channel closing. BTC, LTC.

fee_bumped.description: A replacement paying more to get in sooner, or a child paying its parent's fee. BTC, LTC, DOGE.

mweb_peg_in.description: Coins moving into Litecoin's MWEB extension block. LTC.

large_script.description: A big input script that isn't a multisig spend, usually carrying data. DOGE.

transparent.description: Visible senders, receivers and amounts: no shielded parts. ZEC.

shielding.description: Coins moving from transparent inputs into a shielded pool. ZEC.

deshielding.description: Coins leaving a shielded pool for transparent outputs. ZEC.

shielded.description: Fully private: no transparent inputs or outputs. ZEC.

rune.description: Runes tokens etched, minted or moved: a runestone, or Alkanes; Dunes on Dogecoin. BTC, LTC, DOGE.

bridge.description: Coins crossing to or from another chain: a bridge, or a cross-chain swap. BTC, LTC, DOGE, ZEC.

token.description: Tokens on an older protocol issued or moved: Counterparty, Stamps (SRC-20), Omni; OmniLite on Litecoin. BTC, LTC.

staking.description: Bitcoin staked, unstaked or slashed: Babylon, Core DAO, Stacks stacking. BTC.

anchoring.description: Another chain's checkpoint written into Bitcoin: Stacks block commits, Hemi, Babylon. BTC.

other.description: A kind added later, until it's named here.

vsize.description: Their virtual size in vbytes (bytes on DOGE and ZEC).

fees.description: The fees they paid, in coins; null where they can't be known (as for mweb_peg_in).

blocks.description: The ten newest blocks, newest first.

ProjectedBlock.description: A block projected from the mempool. Fee rates are per virtual byte, in satoshis (BTC, BTCTEST), litoshis (LTC, LTCTEST) or koinu (DOGE, DOGETEST); on Zcash (ZEC, ZECTEST), zatoshis per logical action (ZIP 317).

min_fee_rate_precise.description: min_fee_rate to two decimal places ("0.31"), so rates under one unit show.

fee_unit.description: Zcash only: the rates on this block are zatoshis per logical action (ZIP 317), not per byte.

marginal_fee.description: Zcash only: the ZIP 317 fee per logical action, in zat.

grace_actions.description: Zcash only: the fewest actions a fee pays for, 2.

hashrate.description: Estimated hashes per second (solutions per second on Zcash), as a decimal string.

loading.description: true while the mempool is still being read in: its counts can be low until this turns false.

quote_targets.description: Dogecoin only: fee rates its pools have accepted lately, learned from the last samples blocks with payments. fast, normal and slow are each { fee_rate, within_blocks }: the lowest rate (koinu/vB, like the rates beside it) at which payments got into a block within within_blocks blocks, as often as confidence says (0.95: 95% of the time). null on other networks, and until it has learned.

confidence.description: How often the quotes held, from 0 to 1.

samples.description: Blocks with payments they're learned from.

fee_rate.description: The lowest rate, in koinu/vB, at which payments got into a block within within_blocks blocks, as often as confidence says.

within_blocks.description: How many blocks the quote is for.

currency.description: USD, or the currency you asked for.

as_of.description: When the latest price was taken (Unix time). On the latest price only.

AccountInfo.description: Answered without the status/data envelope, as it always has been.

max_monthly_requests.description: Your plan’s requests a month. Past it, lookups carry on at the free rate and webhooks and streams pause until the month resets.

max_daily_requests.description: Kept for older clients: the monthly number divided by 30. Nothing stops at it.

current_period_ends_at.description: End of the paid period (UTC); null on Free.

today.description: Counted so far today (UTC): API calls, MCP tool calls and webhook notifications.

quota_resets_in_seconds.description: Seconds until the month’s count resets (the 1st, 00:00 UTC).

access.description: read_only keys get 403 on any change to webhooks or buckets.

t.description: Block time (block interval) or the start of the hour, day or minute (Unix time).

v.description: A string for amounts (fees_total, fees_median, supply, price_usd), an object for pool_share, transfers, holder_share, lookalikes, mweb_flows and zcash_pools (mweb_pool is an amount string), otherwise a number; null where there is no data.

provisional.description: Only on the newest hour of price_usd: true while v is the latest price, until that hour's opening price is settled. Absent otherwise, never false.

BucketName.description: Letters, numbers, - and _, up to 64 characters. Unique within your account.

Wallet.description: Only for a bucket filled from a wallet's public key (POST /buckets/{bucket}/xpub). The public key itself is never kept.

running_low.description: True once more than half of a chain's spare addresses are used: send the public key again. Null if it can't be checked just now.

updated_at.description: When the bucket was last filled from the public key (unix time).

used_through.description: The highest used index at the last fill.

next.description: The first index not in the bucket.

spare.description: Spare (unused) addresses after the last used, at the last fill.

spare_left.description: Of those, how many are still unused after the last one used since. Null if it can't be checked just now.

reason.description: too_heavy: the address alone has more than 100,000 transactions of history, or adding it would take the bucket past 1,000,000.

error.description: Details, e.g. how many transactions a too_heavy address has.

tip_height.description: The newest block when the answer was made.

confirmed_sent.description: Everything its addresses have sent, summed over them (a move between two of them counts on both sides, as in confirmed_received).

unconfirmed_txs.description: How many of its transactions are still pending.

first_active.description: Its oldest confirmed transaction's block and time; null without one.

last_active.description: Its newest confirmed transaction's block and time; null without one.

tip_height.description: The newest block when the answer was made.

value_received.description: What the bucket's addresses received in it, together.

value_sent.description: What they sent in it, together.

balance_change.description: The bucket's net gain or loss; a move between two of its own addresses shows just the fee, as a loss.

price.description: The price at the time, as Price; null where there's no price: before the network's price history (Bitcoin's starts 13 Jul 2010), or a block stamped ahead of the clock. Testnets: always 0.

transactions.description: Ten a page: pending first, then newest first.

total.description: How many there are in all.

tip_height.description: The newest block when the answer was made.

unconfirmed_tx_count.description: How many of them are pending.

used.description: Whether it has any history, pending included.

version.description: The bucket's version after this change.

not_member.description: Addresses sent that weren't in it.

hash.description: The transaction that created the output.

index.description: The output's position in that transaction.

block.description: Confirming block height; null while unconfirmed.

p2pk.description: DOGE only: the output is a pay-to-pubkey script of the address's key.

BucketUnspentOutput.description: One of the bucket's unspent outputs: as an address's, without tx_hex.

total.description: How many there are in all.

tip_height.description: The newest block when the answer was made.

WebhookType.description: block.reorged, transaction.replaced and transaction.dropped are delivered alongside these; they aren't created on their own.

network.description: Required unless bucket is given. Free plans: BTCTEST, LTCTEST, DOGETEST or ZECTEST.

url.description: Your HTTPS endpoint, on a public host (not sochain.com).

bucket.description: address.transaction only: watch every address in this bucket.

addresses.description: address.transaction without a bucket: the addresses to watch, up to 1,000 in this call (add more with POST /webhooks/{id}/addresses).

transactions.description: transaction.confirmation: the transaction IDs to track, up to 1,000 in this call (add more with POST /webhooks/{id}/transactions).

notify_at.description: Confirmation counts to notify at, from 0 (first seen) to 100; transaction.confirmation from 1. Defaults: [0, 1] for address.transaction, [1, 2, 3, 6] for transaction.confirmation.

label.description: Optional, for you: shown on the dashboard.

threshold.description: fees.below / fees.above: the fee rate (sat/vB, lit/vB or koinu/vB) to cross.

url.description: A new endpoint: it's checked at once, and the webhook is unverified until it echoes the challenge.

status.description: Pause it, or resume it (a webhook resumes once verified).

label.description: Yours, as the dashboard shows it.

notify_at.description: address.transaction and transaction.confirmation: as on create.

threshold.description: fees.below and fees.above: the fee rate to cross; the alert starts over.

WebhookUpdate.description: Any of these; what isn't sent stays as it is. Any other field is refused with a 400.

label.description: Yours, as the dashboard shows it.

num_addresses.description: Addresses it watches itself (address.transaction without a bucket).

last_event_at.description: When it last sent an event (Unix time); null before its first.

failing_since.description: When its deliveries started failing (Unix time); null while they succeed.

verify_error.description: Why the last endpoint check failed, if it did.

secret.description: Only in the answer to POST /webhooks: the signing secret, shown once.

Deliveries.description: Recent deliveries of this webhook: the event, the attempt count, and how your server answered.

id.description: Unique event ID: de-duplicate on it.

data.description: The details, in v3 field names.

bucket.description: The bucket the address is in, for a bucket's webhook; null otherwise.

balance_change.description: value_received minus value_sent: the address's net change. Negative when it paid out.

wallet.description: Bucket webhooks, when the bucket was filled from a wallet's public key: spare_left as of this event.

BalanceAt.description: The confirmed balance at a past point (with height or time).

height.description: The block the balance is taken at; null for a time before the chain's first block.

block_hash.description: That block's hash. If a reorg replaces it, ask again.

confirmed.description: The confirmed balance at the end of that block. Pending transactions never count.

tip_height.description: The newest block when the answer was made.

HistoryPage.description: Paging and filter fields of the filtered form.

next_cursor.description: Send it back as cursor for the next page; null when there's nothing more. A short page, even an empty one, with a cursor isn't the end.

from_height.description: The range searched, as blocks; null for an open end.

tip_height.description: The newest block when the walk began. To pick up new transactions later, start at from_height = tip_height − 6 and skip IDs you already have.

reorged.description: Only after a reorg under the cursor: the walk started over from its top, so some rows come again.

fork_height.description: With reorged: the lowest replaced block, or null when it's more than 8 blocks deep.

TransactionsCsv.description: CSV with a header row: time_utc, block, txid, direction (in, out or none), received, sent, net, price_usd, net_usd (net at the USD price, to the cent). Amounts are exact decimals.

BucketBalanceAt.description: The bucket's confirmed total at a past point (with height or time), for the addresses in it now.

funded_addresses.description: Addresses that held a balance then.

members.description: With members=true: each address's confirmed balance then.

tip_height.description: The newest block when the answer was made.

height.description: The newest block the list reflects.

supply.description: Every confirmed coin: what share_of_supply divides by.

address.description: null for coins in outputs with no address (pay-to-public-key, bare multisig).

rank.description: Exact within the top 10,000; null below that or below the rich list's minimum.

resolution_blocks.description: 1: every balance exact at its interval's end; 128: a balance can lag it by up to 128 blocks (received and sent are always exact).

external_available.description: Whether received_external and sent_external are filled in. Not yet: they will be, in this same form.

t.description: Interval start (UTC); the last point is the newest block's time.

v.description: Confirmed balance at the interval's end.

received.description: Came in during the interval, change included.

received_external.description: What came in from other addresses, leaving out coins it moved to itself; null while external_available is false.

sent_external.description: What went out to other addresses, leaving out coins it moved to itself; null while external_available is false.

building.description: true while the check is catching up on the network's history.
